items.markup:
The Letter / Chapter 1

On the Cliff

Eleanor discovers a letter revealing her father may not be who he claims.

Choose a scene beat

Eleanor Blackwood had always known this day would come.

The letter in her pocket—crumpled now from being read a dozen times—confirmed what she’d long suspected: her father was not who he claimed to be.

It was only Thomas, the relief keeper, with his coat buttoned wrong and his hair full of weather. He stopped when he saw her face.

“You’ve found it, then,” he said.

There were eighty-seven steps to the lamp room. Eleanor counted them twice.

She had climbed eighty-eight every night since she was old enough to carry the oil.

items.title: Feature sequence
items.description: Full-width alternating rows, hairline-divided and numbered with a print folio.
items.source: Redesign / latest feature alignment + four product images
items.usage: Features read as a sequence, not a matrix of tiles — a hard rule in the design guide, because equal tiles produce ragged heights and dead space beside a text-only entry. Add pw-feature--reverse to every second row so the figure alternates sides. Product figures take the mounted-print treatment and are cropped to fit, so check a source ratio clears the slot; wrap an image in pw-image-frame only when the whole frame must stay visible. Each row has exactly two children: a prose wrapper and the figure.

items.description: Hairlines establish the rhythm. Native disclosure behavior keeps answers close without hiding the question.
items.usage: Use for secondary explanations, not the main navigation or primary message. Each summary is a complete question. Multiple answers may remain open; no JavaScript is needed.
items.markup:
Can I use these components without a framework?

Yes. Load the local fonts, tokens, and website stylesheet, then use the HTML markup. Add the optional script for interactive patterns.

Does this change the application’s design?

No. Website styles are opt-in and scoped. The canonical tokens and existing application examples remain available separately.

Where should I change a shared color?

Edit the canonical tokens.css file, regenerate the mirrors, and release a new package version. Do not maintain a second palette in a consumer.
